summary: Postmortem follow-up after Lyra experienced sustained token latency increase and partial degradation during a Dedicated pool autoscaling event. Root cause narrowed to race in autoscaler leading to KV cache invalidation and an unexpected warmup cost on restart; mitigations proposed and next steps agreed.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-11 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM); Sofia (Lyra), Ethan (Lyra SRE), Priya (Lyra Security), Marcus (Lyra Infra)
Links: incident doc https://redwood.app/incident/CR-49821, repro spreadsheet, shared perf logs (link redacted)

00:00 Maya (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh quick roll call then we'll jump in. Sofia?
00:06 Sofia (Customer): hi, Sofia here. we have Ethan, Priya, Marcus on. thanks for doing this.
00:12 Maya: cool. quick goal of today's  make sure action items are clear, share timelines and next steps, and give you the final RCA notes.
00:20 Liam (SE): yeah, i'll start with a short timeline and what we reproduced in our env. apologies for the noise  this is a bit rough audio.
00:30 Ethan (Customer): that's fine. we're mostly interested in root cause and mitigation. cost impact and potential longer term changes.
00:36 Liam: ok timeline recap  on 2026-08-04 at ~02:10 UTC you hit a scale event in your dedicated gpu pool, autoscaler triggered new nodes, during node join we observed kv cache invalidation for a subset of shards which caused cache warmups and tokens spiking, we saw 5-7x token latency increases for certain request patterns.
00:57 Priya: just to clarify when you say KV cache you mean the prefix cache? we saw requests stall for up to 11s for some sessions.
01:05 Liam: yes, the prefix/K-V cache  in logs it appears a race between the autoscaler reassigning shards and the runtime's cache restore. basically cache was evicted then restored in a way that wasn't refilled quickly. plus a degenerate routing decision sent some DP requests to a cold node.
01:22 Marcus: there were also spikes in network attach time  EBS attach timings coincided with the worst latencies. could that be a factor?
01:30 Liam: good call; we correlated the attach timings and they overlapped, but the primary consistent signal is the cache miss/warmup. network attach amplified the tail.
01:40 Sofia: what triggered the autoscaler in the first place? we saw a traffic spike from an internal batch job, but it shouldn't have required that many nodes.
01:48 Maya: our telemetry shows a burst in seq length and concurrent sessions that matched your account acl metrics; the policy did scale. we think the autoscaler threshold was too aggressive for that workload profile.
02:00 Ethan: we also saw a bad retry loop in our client that probably multiplied requests during the early minutes. so there's some shared blame.
02:10 Priya: from security perspective, were any logs missing? we requested audit trails for the period.
02:16 Jordan (CSM): we captured audit logs; we're attaching them to the incident doc. nothing indicates unauthorized access, it's operational only.
02:24 Maya: ok immediate mitigations we executed: 1) rolled back the autoscaler policy to conservative thresholds, 2) pinned routing for critical routes to warm nodes to avoid cold starts, 3) increased burst capacity on the Dedicated pool to absorb future spikes. these were applied by 02:45 UTC on 2026-08-04.
02:44 Marcus: the pinning helped; we saw tail latency drop back to baseline within ~20 minutes after the rollback.
02:52 Liam: for the RCA technical detail  the autoscaler reassigns shards using the new placement algorithm; when a node leaves and rejoins there was a path where cache restore calls were retried in parallel and some namespaces got replaced before their cached entries were persisted to shared storage, so subsequent requests hit cold paths. it's a concurrency edge.
03:15 Sofia: is this specific to our deployment or a general risk in Dedicated?
03:20 Liam: it's a risk for workloads with high session locality and heavy prefix reuse; customers with similar profiles could be impacted  we're treating this as a product reliability bug and have a mitigation plan in the runtime.
03:30 Priya: what's the timeline for a fix? and will you provide a security attestation?
03:36 Maya: short term fix is a safe-guard in the autoscaler to delay reassignment until cache checkpoint completes  we have a hotfix patch and plan to roll it next week in a canary region. longer term we'll add stronger cache checkpointing and improved lifecycle hooks.
03:52 Liam: actionables from our engineering side: implement the checkpoint handshake in the autoscaler (P1), add better metrics to alert on cache miss rate (P2), and run focused load tests with your captured traffic shapes (P1).
04:08 Ethan: load test schedule? we'd like a joint run where we replay traffic including the seq length distribution.
04:15 Liam: yes, we'll repro with your anonymized traces; asking Lyra to provide traces and a couple of sample prompts.
04:22 Sofia: we'll share trace bundle by 2026-08-12.
04:26 Marcus: on the Dedicated capacity/contract side, we're interested in the burst option you applied and pricing for guaranteed capacity for critical routes.
04:34 Maya: i'll send options  dedicated reserved vs burst add-on, and a design where critical routes can be pinned to reserved warm nodes.
04:42 Priya: can we get SOC2 audit snippets about node lifecycle events and key rotation? we need that for our compliance team.
04:50 Jordan: yes we'll include audit-logs exports and KMS rotation details, and the postmortem will include a security appendix.
04:58 Ethan: one question  you mentioned a 'fallback to hosted model variant' during capacity issues. can you remind us how that would work?
05:05 Liam: sure. runtime can route to a smaller but compatible model variant in another region or hosted tier; it's an SLO-tradeoff but keeps availability. we suggested adding a policy that prefers regional warm nodes first then falls back.
05:20 Sofia: do you have any benchmarks on latency delta for fallback models?
05:24 Liam: we do  rough numbers: baseline 70-90ms p50 per token on your config, fallback was 150-250ms p50 and higher p95; we'll attach the benchmark sheet. (audio glitch) sorry, list link in incident doc.
05:38 Maya: ok let's recap next steps  Maya will share postmortem with full timeline and security appendix by 2026-08-13; Liam will run repro and attach perf logs by 2026-08-18; Jordan will coordinate exec readout by 2026-08-15; Lyra will share traces by 2026-08-12.
05:58 Priya: that works. also please include any mitigation playbooks we can call in the future (how to pin routes, rollback autoscale, contact playbook).
06:05 Maya: yes, we'll add runbook steps and an ops checklist.
06:10 Ethan: regarding longer term reliability improvements, will you consider a config that preserves prefix cache across node replacement without full checkpointing?
06:18 Liam: we're evaluating two approaches: incremental checkpointing and a shared cache backing store; both have tradeoffs for latency and cost. we prefer incremental checkpointing combined with a quick warmup path.
06:30 Sofia: final ask  can we get a short SLA credit review for the window of impact?
06:36 Jordan: we'll open a credit request and route through your account, need to confirm the exact impact window and metrics.
06:42 Maya: thanks everyone. any other items?
06:45 Marcus: nothing else. appreciate the quick work.
06:48 Maya: great, we'll follow up in the agreed dates. meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription: some words may be imperfect (K V cache spelled K-V or K V, SAM-el for SAML in one exchange). crosstalk and short audio dropouts around 05:24 and 03:00.

End transcript.
